card.title: Crisis-correlation risk budgeting with trend gates, drawdown floor and staggered daily rebalancing
card.pitch: Budget risk across growth, rates and real-asset classes using stress-day covariance, shift budget from rates to real assets when stock-bond correlation turns positive, halve downtrending assets into cash, and trade a fifth of the target gap each day.
card.mechanism: Stress set: worst 50 of the last 500 days of equal-weight 10-ETF return. Sigma = 0.5*(stress covariance about its own mean) + 0.5*(500-day covariance). Class budgets: Growth (five equity/REIT ETFs) 1/3; Rates (UST, IG, TIPS: duration assets) (1-c)/3; Real (gold, commodities) (1+c)/3, with c = clip(250-day correlation of equal-weight Growth and Rates baskets, 0, 0.5). Equal within class; ERC weights w. Cash arises from the vol cap k, trend gate g_i (0.5 below SMA200) and a CPPI drawdown floor m = clip(6*(1-0.8*HWM/NAV), 0, 1), never renormalised away. Target T = k*m*g*w. Daily, a fifth of the gap to T is traded (a rolling 20% sleeve), capped so turnover holds by construction.
card.rationale: Correlations rise in sell-offs (Longin-Solnik 2001), so full-sample risk parity understates crisis risk. Trend gates cut drawdowns (Faber 2007; Hurst et al. 2017); a CPPI floor bounds losses (Black-Perold 1992). Staggering reduces timing luck (Hoffstein et al. 2020). Hand estimate, not backtested: net 4-5% CAGR at about 5% volatility; 2008, 2020, 2022 drawdowns roughly 6-12%.
assumptions: 50 stress days with 50% shrinkage give a stable matrix
failure_modes: Unlevered book lags equity bull runs
card.cheapest_test: Backtest 2008-2025 with 5 and 10 bp costs; ablate stress covariance, gate, floor, dynamic budgets. Report 2008/2020/2022 drawdowns, CAGR, maximum weekly turnover. Kill if drawdown exceeds 15%, net CAGR trails cash by under 2 points, or stress covariance adds nothing.
card.spec: Gap G = T - actual weights. Trade x = G*min(0.2, cap/(0.5*sum|G|)); cap = min(0.035, 0.195 - turnover realised this calendar week incl. drift). k = min(1, 6%/sqrt(w'Sigma w)). ERC by Newton, tol 1e-8; stress ties: earlier day. Holidays: no catch-up.

responses.response: The critique is correct: renormalising after the gate cancels it. The gate now multiplies weights after the vol cap, T = k*m*g*w, with k = min(1, 6%/sigma(w)) computed on the UNGATED ERC weights (which sum to 1, so k <= 1 and there is no levering). The residual is cash and is never rescaled. A uniform gate of 0.5 now halves exposure: all assets below SMA200 gives 50% invested. Exposure is cut by the gate itself, not only by the lagging vol target and the drawdown rule.

Same defect as critic-003-01, same fix: k is computed before the gate and no 1/sum(w) renormalisation follows. Algebra: with uniform gate g, exposure = k*g*sum(w) = k*g, which scales with g. Partial gating leaves cash equal to k*sum_i (1-g_i) w_i. This now matches Faber/Hurst, where a signal-off asset moves to cash.

Accepted that 20/7 = 2.9 sigma was a weak sanity check and that a 13-17% estimate left too little margin. Three changes. (1) The drawdown rule is now a stateless CPPI floor at 0.8*HWM with multiplier 6, so target exposure is continuous: m starts falling at about 4% drawdown, is about 0.5 at 12.7%, and is 0 at 20%. There is no 12% trigger with 8 points of headroom. (2) Unlevered vol is about 4.5-5%, not 7%, because ERC weights put roughly 60-65% in low-vol duration (my hand calculation with vols of 5-6% for UST/IG/TIPS gives about 65% rates weight). That lowers iid MDD (the sigma^2/(2 mu) scaling gives roughly 8-11%), and the floor truncates the tail. (3) 2022 is the binding case: the bond leg (IEF -15%, LQD -18%, TIP -12%, approximate) would lose about 9-10% of NAV at 65% duration weight, but the correlation rule can cut Rates from 1/3 to 1/6 of risk (weight about 40%), the SMA200 gate halves bonds by early 2022, and the floor engages from -4%. My hand estimate is 7-12%. Not backtested; the kill criterion is a backtested drawdown above 15%. Gap risk is conceded: CPPI guarantees the floor only if the loss between trades stays under 1/6 of exposed assets, and the 3.5%/day trade cap means a 2020-type week can arrive faster than exposure falls.

Points (a), (c) and (d) accepted: the two-state 12%/8% brake, its 3.5% vol target (not binding for a 4-6% vol book) and the 0.92 HWM re-entry are removed. The CPPI floor is continuous, acts from about 4% drawdown, has no re-entry threshold, and restores exposure smoothly as NAV approaches HWM, so there is no multi-year half-risk state; a partial drag while below HWM remains as a known cost. Point (b), execution lag, is conceded as a real limit: at 3.5% per day, going from 100% to 50% exposure takes about 14 trading days. Mitigation is only partial: the floor starts scaling at 4% not 12%, and the book is mostly low-volatility bonds, so a 20% loss inside 14 days needs an extreme joint shock. A March 2020-type shock is the dominant residual risk.

Correct that budgets were constant, so nothing moved to gold or cash, and that TIPS is a duration asset. Fixes: (1) TIPS moves into a Rates class with UST and IG (three duration ETFs); Real is gold and commodities only; Growth stays five ETFs including REITs. (2) Budgets are now dynamic: c = clip(250-day correlation of the Growth and Rates baskets, 0, 0.5); Rates get (1-c)/3 and Real (1+c)/3, so at c = 0.5 Rates fall to 1/6 and Real rise to 1/2. Real is capped at 1/2 of risk, so no class exceeds 1/2 by rule. (3) Cash arises through k, m and g; I no longer claim that budget moves to cash. The 250-day window responds faster than the 500-day matrix; the remaining lag is conceded and partly offset by the gate.

g was undefined and is now defined. T is the global target and G = T - actual weights (including drift) is the gap; each day a fifth of G is traded (a rolling 20% sleeve, equivalent to rebalancing one equal sleeve on its weekday), scaled so the one-way trade is at most 3.5% of NAV. Sleeve NAVs no longer exist, so they cannot drift apart. Slow chasing of the signal on days when the cap binds is conceded; it binds mainly in large regime moves, where smoothing is acceptable.

Accepted: 5 x 4% = 20% left no margin and drift was ignored. The daily cap is now 3.5% (5 x 3.5 = 17.5%), plus a hard weekly budget: cap_d = min(0.035, 0.195 - realised turnover so far this calendar week), where realised turnover is the running sum of 0.5*sum|weight change| between consecutive closes (trades plus price drift). That sum upper-bounds the net weekly definition by the triangle inequality, so the 20% gate holds by construction rather than by a statistical margin. Three-days rule: the gap is non-zero every day because volatility, correlation and SMA inputs change daily, so a trade occurs on every trading day unless the weekly budget is exhausted; Monday to Wednesday trades total at most 10.5%, so exhaustion before Wednesday would need more than 9% of drift in two days, which is implausible even in 2020. Holiday weeks trade on all remaining days.

Accepted. The stress covariance is now computed about the stress subset's own mean (a conditional covariance), removing the mean-outer-product term. I also tightened the stress set to the worst 50 (10%) of 500 days so it differs more from S_500, and keep 50% shrinkage against estimation noise (N/T = 0.2). Forbes-Rigobon selection bias in conditional correlations is real and remains; I keep it deliberately as a conservative upward bias, and the ablation against full-sample covariance in the cheapest test checks whether it adds value. Longin-Solnik is extreme-value evidence and serves as motivation, not proof.
